cls: Antiviral - nucleotide analogue RNA-dependent RNA polymerase inhibitor
pharm: An intravenous antiviral nucleotide prodrug that inhibits SARS-CoV-2 RNA polymerase, used to treat COVID-19

summary: Remdesivir is an intravenous nucleotide-analogue prodrug that inhibits the SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, terminating viral RNA synthesis. It is approved for the treatment of COVID-19 in adult and paediatric patients (including infants) who are hospitalised or who are non-hospitalised with mild-to-moderate disease at high risk of progression. The usual adult regimen is a 200 mg loading dose on day 1 followed by 100 mg once daily, with total duration of 3 days (non-hospitalised high-risk) up to 5-10 days depending on illness severity and need for ventilation/ECMO. Key safety concerns are hypersensitivity and infusion-related reactions (slow or stop the infusion if they occur) and transaminase (ALT) elevation, so liver tests should be checked and the drug stopped for marked ALT rise or signs of liver injury. It is given by infusion over 30-120 minutes and is generally well tolerated.
indications: Treatment of COVID-19 in adults and paediatric patients (including neonates at least 7 days old and weighing at least 1.5 kg) who are hospitalised, OR non-hospitalised with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 and at high risk of progression to severe disease, including hospitalisation or death

moa: Remdesivir is a phosphoramidate prodrug of an adenosine nucleotide analogue. Inside cells it is metabolised to the active nucleoside triphosphate, which is incorporated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) into nascent SARS-CoV-2 RNA. Incorporation causes delayed chain termination of viral RNA synthesis, inhibiting viral replication. Because it targets the viral polymerase rather than a host enzyme, it has selective antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2 and related RNA viruses.

absolute: Known severe hypersensitivity to remdesivir or any component of the formulation
relative: Significant hepatic impairment or marked baseline ALT elevation (use only if benefit outweighs risk)
monitor: Signs of hypersensitivity and infusion-related reactions

preg: There are limited but reassuring data on remdesivir in pregnancy. It may be used during pregnancy when the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; COVID-19 in pregnancy carries significant maternal and fetal risk that should be weighed.
lact: Limited data show low transfer into breast milk and low oral bioavailability in the infant. The benefits of breastfeeding are generally considered to outweigh any small risk; decisions should be individualised.
renal: Per current labelling, remdesivir can be used across the spectrum of renal function, including patients on dialysis, with no dosage adjustment required; earlier restrictions related to the sulfobutylether-beta-cyclodextrin (SBECD) excipient have been removed.
hepatic: Remdesivir can raise transaminases. It should be used in patients with hepatic impairment only if the potential benefit outweighs the risk. Perform hepatic laboratory testing before and during treatment; consider discontinuation if ALT rises to >=5 times the upper limit of normal or if transaminase elevation is accompanied by signs of liver inflammation or rising bilirubin/INR.

moderate: Chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine - may reduce the antiviral activity of remdesivir; concomitant use not recommended
minor: Potential interactions with strong CYP inducers (e.g. rifampicin) that could lower remdesivir exposure - coadministration not recommended
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; minimise if there is concern about hepatic effects
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate ALT/AST and prothrombin time; monitor hepatic tests and coagulation as indicated

counsel: This antiviral is given by a drip to treat COVID-19; it works best when started early
Tell the staff straight away if you feel unwell during the infusion - flushing, itching, breathlessness, swelling or dizziness
Blood tests will check your liver during treatment
Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine or right-upper-abdominal pain after treatment
Let your team know all other medicines you take, especially chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine
pk: Active triphosphate forms intracellularly soon after infusion; antiviral effect during the treatment course
Parent remdesivir peaks at end of infusion; rapidly metabolised to active and metabolite forms
Parent remdesivir terminal half-life about 1 hour; active intracellular metabolite (GS-441524 nucleoside) half-life roughly 24-27 hours
Once-daily dosing maintains intracellular active metabolite over the treatment course
Lyophilised powder stored at controlled room temperature; reconstituted/diluted solution per label (refrigerate and use within specified time)
pearls: First antiviral approved for COVID-19; inhibits viral RNA polymerase (RdRp) and works best started early in illness
Key safety signals: hypersensitivity/infusion reactions (slow or stop infusion) and transaminase (ALT) elevation - check LFTs
Stop for ALT >=5x ULN or transaminase rise with signs of liver inflammation/rising bilirubin or INR
No renal dose adjustment is now required (earlier cyclodextrin-related restriction removed); usable in dialysis
Avoid concomitant chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine, which may reduce its antiviral activity
Give only intravenously over 30-120 minutes; duration is 3 days (outpatient high-risk) up to 5-10 days when hospitalised
missed: Remdesivir is given as scheduled daily infusions by healthcare staff during a defined course, so patients do not self-administer or make up doses. If a dose is delayed, the care team will adjust the schedule.
overdose: There is no specific experience with remdesivir overdose and no specific antidote. Management is supportive, with monitoring of vital signs, hepatic and renal function, and treatment of any hypersensitivity or organ toxicity that arises.
